news.title: Socceroos on the move: Lucas Herrington headlines post-World Cup transfers | Joey Lynch
news.lede: The defender is set to become one of Australia’s most expensive players with a Premier League deal nearly done while some international teammates have already made moves. Lucas Herrington, fresh off becoming the youngest Australian to start a game at a men’s World Cup, is set to become the second-most expensive footballer in Australian history with a move to newly-promoted Premier League side Hull City. Latest reports suggest a fee of approximately £12.6m ($24.1m), with a further £4.4m ($8.4m) in add-ons, which comes in just shy of the Australian record of £15m plus £5m in add-ons ($38.3m in total) that Leicester paid Stoke City to sign Harry Souttar in 2023. It would set a new selling high-water mark for his current club, Colorado Rapids, and eclipses the decade-old record Hull set when they paid just over £10m for Ryan Mason.

news.title: Pressure on Gianni Infantino increases as Uefa members prepare to oppose re-election
news.lede: European nations to withdraw letters of support for Fifa president. Appetite to ensure Infantino is quickly removed from post. European countries are planning to increase the pressure on Gianni Infantino with a mass withdrawal of letters supporting his re-election as Fifa president. Infantino’s reign is in severe peril after the collapse of his privately backed scheme to sell off chunks of the World Cup, which was largely scuppered when Uefa member associations threatened to boycott future Fifa competitions.

news.title: Five lessons for startups from football World Cup
news.lede: I landed in Seattle a day before the FIFA World Cup 2026 began. For the next 40 days, the city turned into a giant football stadium. National flags appeared everywhere, strangers speaking different languages vehemently debated offsides over free-flowing beer and communicated perfectly through groans and screams at public screenings in pubs, bars and waterfronts. Beneath the celebrations was a massive management operation startups can learn from.

news.title: A case for a Windies football team
news.lede: After the month of World Cup football, with a match playing almost every day, I am so having withdrawal. It is not that I am so into football. This is like the Summer and Winter Olympics. Even if it is not your sport, it is difficult to resist the athletics at such a high level, occurring only once every four years.

news.title: Is Concacaf ready to make challenge to FIFA presidency?
news.lede: When news broke that FIFA was scrapping its commercialization plans, there was rampant celebration globally. Now, though, there is likely to be a fallout from the proposal and its driver, FIFA president Gianni Infantino. Within a statement released by Concacaf, it sure seems like the organization could be making a run at the throne: > Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations welcome the withdrawal of the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). > The Confederation also commends its 41 Member Associations and the wider football family for the courage and unity they have shown this week.

news.title: FIFA scrap World Cup sell-off plan after backlash
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA “will not proceed” with plans to sell stakes in a company which would run the commercial and operational aspects of its competitions, a statement from president Gianni Infantino said. The plan, which would include the men’s and women’s World Cups, has been rejected by three continental confederations with UEFA insisting its nations would boycott FIFA events.

news.title: UEFA declare loss of confidence in Infantino after World Cup sell-off controversy
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA president Gianni Infantino has “lost the confidence” of UEFA over a plan to sell stakes in a World Cup company to private investors, the European football governing body has said. Infantino announced overnight that the plan would not proceed after three confederations rejected it, with UEFA going further and saying it would boycott FIFA competitions until the proposal was scrapped.

news.title: British prime minister says Infantino is not the right man to lead FIFA
news.lede: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Sunday that FIFA President Gianni Infantino was not the right man to lead world soccer’s governing body in the latest fallout from the now abandoned plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. “I do not believe that he is the right man to lead football forward on the world stage," Burnham said. “The plan that was put forward was offensive to many people, football people, around the world, and it can’t be the case that we just move on and forget that, it wasn’t acceptable." On Saturday, European soccer's governing body UEFA said it had lost confidence in FIFA’s leadership — possibly paving the way for a challenge to Infantino’s presidency.
